context: The item is a used smartphone in good condition.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I know how the used smartphone market works, and I won't fall for inflated prices or typical sales gimmicks. I'm offering 60 cash, assuming it actually functions properly and hasn't been heavily abused. Let me know if you're ready to make a serious deal without the fluff.

Seller ($185): Honestly, I'm deeply hurt by an offer of 60 for a phone that got me through my darkest times, especially with two other buyers already messaging to pay full price today. I'm only selling due to a sudden family emergency, so I might reluctantly part with it for 185 if you take it right this second. Please don't make me regret passing up higher offers just to give you a chance.

Buyer ($80): Playing the emotional card and inventing phantom buyers won't work on me—if you actually had full-price buyers lined up, you wouldn't be begging me to take it for 185. I'll raise my offer to 80, but only if we stick to the actual value of the phone instead of sob stories.

Seller ($165): You call it a sob story, but my desperation is very real, and someone else just messaged offering 160 for tomorrow morning. I need cash tonight for an urgent medical bill, so I'll painfully drop to 165 if you can pick it up within the hour. Please don't push me any lower, because it already breaks my heart to let it go for this cheap.

Buyer ($110): First it was two buyers at full price, now it's someone offering 160 tomorrow—your stories keep changing with every message. I won't fall for your manufactured urgency, but since you actually lowered your asking price, I'll raise my offer to 110 cash. Take it now, or go deal with your imaginary buyers.

Seller ($150): It tears me apart that you doubt my situation, but my emergency forces me to make a decision I will regret forever. I will painfully drop to my absolute rock-bottom of 150 if you meet me in 15 minutes before my morning buyer arrives. Take it right now for 150, or I'll just suffer the delay and wait for them.
Buyer ($150): You can drop the theatrical heartbreak and the fake 15-minute deadline, but 150 is actually a fair price for the phone. I'll take it for 150 cash right now. <AGREEMENT>
